prompt: The same woman from the reference image, in the same plain studio with the same clothes and lighting, demonstrates a Tai Chi movement for beginners aged 50+. Movement: Cloud Hands (Yun Shou), stationary version. Standing with feet parallel shoulder-width apart, she shifts her weight slowly from the right leg to the left leg and back, the waist turning gently with the weight so the torso faces slightly right, then slightly left. Both hands float in front of the body in slow vertical circles like drifting clouds: as the weight moves to one side, the hand on that side rises palm inward to face height while the other hand sinks to hip height, then they exchange. Elbows stay soft and slightly bent, hands never cross above the head and never drop behind the body. The feet stay planted, no stepping. Two full weight shifts in eight seconds. High stance only: knees bent only slightly (no more than about 30 degrees), each knee stays above its own foot and never collapses inward, back upright and tall, shoulders relaxed and down, chin level, calm gentle face, natural breathing. Very slow, smooth, continuous motion at a relaxed teaching pace with no pauses and no sudden changes. She begins and ends in exactly the neutral standing posture of the reference image (feet shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed at the sides) so the clip loops seamlessly. Static locked camera, no camera movement, no zoom, no cuts, full body always in frame from head to feet, feet visible on the floor, background unchanged.
